film: Flipkart x Autopilot: Andheri East, the shortlist (script draft 4)
settings_reason: Both settings passed speech-to-text on both lines. A (speed 0.95) came out with slightly wider pitch movement (11.3-13.5 vs 10.7-11.9 semitones, 10th-90th percentile) but that is within take-to-take variation: A's opening line was actually shorter than B's. The difference that matters is pace on the long line: A spoke l02 at 2.75 words a second (10.9 s in a 12 s slot), B at 2.99 (10.0 s). Over the whole script (about 365 spoken words) A projects to about 143 s of voice plus breaths against 130 s of script slots, past the 2:10 picture and the 2:20 bed; B projects to about 132 s. B is also the more energetic read the founder asked for, and still well below the Reliable film's rushed 3.7 words a second at default speed. The opener (under black, 8 s slot) came out at 4.2 words a second in both takes, so its tts text carries one written 0.6 s pause between its two sentences; the words are unchanged.
continuity: each request carries previous_text and next_text (the neighbouring lines)
timings: times in each line are seconds from the start of its own file; slot_s is the script time slot in film seconds

lines.stt_notes: Speech-to-text never wrote 'Andheri East' for this line on its own (6 takes: 'And here he is', 'And here east', 'Under East', 'And here is', 'And there is'; respellings 'Undheri' and Devanagari 'अंधेरी' and a slower read did not change it). Control: the 'Andheri East' cut out of l02, which speech-to-text writes correctly inside its sentence, is heard as 'Under East' when isolated. So the failure is the speech-to-text's need for context, not her pronunciation. With l02's 'Flipkart asked us for space in' spliced in front, every take is heard as 'Andheri East. Let's choose it together'. Take 2 is used (plain spelling, the chosen settings, a 0.5 s pause).
